method: sum of gzip -9 over each module in the route's rel="modulepreload" list, per file, never concatenated
tolerance_basis: 4 builds of identical source, route /, 2026-08-25, this repo: 49193 / 49198 / 49198 / 49205. Range 12 B, and the cause is named - SvelteKit stamps a version string into the entry chunk. 64 B is 5.3x that range; four samples underestimate a true range, so the multiple is the margin. Derived, not measured. If a build ever fails inside 64 B, re-derive it from more builds and more routes rather than nudging it.

/.why: Up for the lens chip on an item's eyebrow. LensChips.svelte plus the six display names in src/lib/payload/lenses.ts reach every route that renders an item. Measured 2026-08-30 on this tree, one session, one node: / 52,584 -> 52,891 (+307), /<date>/ 51,817 -> 52,127 (+310), /<date>/<topic>/ 51,908 -> 52,221 (+313), /archive/ 53,218 -> 53,525 (+307). The control is in the same run and needs no second build: /404, /console/ and /evals/ render no item and all three read inside the 64 B tolerance against their committed records, so this machine agrees with the record on every untouched route and the delta is the change rather than the toolchain. The names are held in a module rather than passed through `data` because `data` repeats all six inside every prerendered day page, and a day page is the heaviest thing we publish - /<date>/ is 350,597 gzipped bytes of HTML against 52,127 of first-load JavaScript. Confirm against the CI site job before trusting the absolute figures: a local Windows build has read 81 to 87 B under CI on every route before now.

/404.why: Runtime and app shell and nothing route-specific. This is the floor every other route sits on. It fell 105 B in the same chunk re-cut that raised /: one module left this route's preload list. Control on this tree: 40,858 B. Every route pays a few tens of bytes for the chart engine existing, without carrying any of it. Measured 2026-08-29 on one machine in one session, origin/main built first and this branch second: / 49,715 -> 49,738, /404 40,769 -> 40,802, /<date>/ 49,591 -> 49,610, /<date>/<topic>/ 49,684 -> 49,702, /archive/ 51,114 -> 51,137, /evals/ 41,725 -> 41,754. On the CI runner, a newer node, the same difference reads 72 to 77 B, which is what pushed /404 2 B past the 64 B tolerance and is why these records moved at all. The module count is unchanged on every route - /404 carries the same 14 modules before and after - so this is not chart code reaching a reading page. It is the shared entry chunk: adding a lazily-imported chunk grows the client manifest the entry embeds, and every route preloads the entry. That is the price of the engine being lazy rather than eager, and it is the right side of the trade: the alternative puts 153,204 B on the console first load instead of 30 B on each page. Up for the icon set. Fifteen glyphs, 2,128 B of marks, reach every route as one generated module because a component names an icon by id and the lookup cannot be tree-shaken on a dynamic key. Measured 2026-08-29 on this tree: / +1,897, /404 +1,771, /<date>/ +1,900, /<date>/<topic>/ +1,900, /archive/ +1,833, /console/ +1,404, /evals/ +1,775. The alternative measured against it was an inline sprite referenced by <use>, which costs no JavaScript at all but puts about 700 B of gzipped markup into every prerendered document - and /404 had 37 B of headroom under its ceiling, so that arm would have had to raise the one ceiling whose whole purpose is keeping the error page tiny. The bytes go where there is room for them. Up for installability. The shell gained a manifest link, an apple-touch-icon link and two media-scoped theme-color tags, plus the code that writes one unconditional theme-color from the resolved background - measured 2026-08-29, 126 to 131 B of first-load JS on every route and 271 B of gzipped markup in every prerendered document. Both are shell costs and neither is avoidable per page: app.html is shared. The apple-touch link in particular cannot be dropped, because Safari probes the ORIGIN root for that filename and this site is served from a project path. DOWN 127 to 150 B, and one module lighter, for the chart vocabulary landing on the console. Measured 2026-08-29: / 51,762 -> 51,613, /404 42,703 -> 42,576, /<date>/ 51,637 -> 51,487, /<date>/<topic>/ 51,728 -> 51,580, /archive/ 53,097 -> 52,961, /evals/ 43,658 -> 43,530, each losing a module from its preload list. The cause is chunking rather than deletion: with five more console-only chart modules in the graph, the bundler stopped hoisting the Chart component into the shared chunk and put it in the console chunk where its only callers now are. The ratchet is two-sided on purpose, so a route getting lighter is recorded rather than left as slack for the next regression to land inside. Up 72 to 149 B for the Panel and StatusChip components entering the shared graph. Measured 2026-08-29: / +72, /404 +149, /<date>/ +72, /<date>/<topic>/ +73, /archive/ +134, /evals/ +145. Only the console draws them, but they are small enough that the bundler keeps them in the shared chunk rather than splitting a chunk for two components. Re-derived 2026-08-29 at the close of the design-system reset, from FIVE builds of identical source taking the HEAVIEST per route rather than the mean - a mean fires on half of all builds. The spread over those five was 13 to 15 B per route, against a 64 B tolerance. This is the first record in this file derived after every sibling row merged rather than while one was still in flight, which is the mistake that set a ceiling from a stacked branch on 2026-08-27 and had it fire 3 days early. Up for the console window control. Every route carries 105 to 111 B of it without rendering any of it: the control is one more client module, and SvelteKit embeds the client manifest in the entry chunk that every route preloads. The module count is unchanged on every route, so this is the manifest and not chart code reaching a reading page. Measured 2026-08-29 on the CI runner, node 22, run 33262132249, against the records this change started from: / 52,474 -> 52,584, /404 42,736 -> 42,841, /<date>/ 51,707 -> 51,817, /<date>/<topic>/ 51,801 -> 51,908, /archive/ 53,109 -> 53,218, /console/ 76,716 -> 78,479, /evals/ 43,687 -> 43,798. Recorded from CI rather than from a developer machine on purpose: the same change measured on node 24.12.0 read 176 B a route instead of 108, and origin/main itself read 81 to 87 B under every committed record there, so a local number is not the number this gate compares against.

/console/.why: Runtime and shell plus the console route: hand-written SVG charts and the d3-scale and d3-array arithmetic behind them, the stage-timing decade axis, the compression scatter that places its articles in the browser, the Charts table, the What the model did table, and the chart engine bridge - the Chart component, the option builders and the token-to-sentinel swap. Up 1,026 B from the 80,831 this record held, for the site-size row: the per-article cost series with its median-and-one-deviation band and its flagged points, the runway arithmetic, the three states the card has to tell apart, and the fill track KpiCard gained. About 22 B of that is the toolchain rather than the change, so the change itself is close to 1,004 B. The control is in the same build and needed no second run: every one of the six untouched routes read 20 to 24 B above its own committed record on this machine and this node (/ +23, /404 +24, /<date>/ +21, /<date>/<topic>/ +21, /archive/ +20, /evals/ +23), so this machine agrees with the record everywhere the change did not reach. That per-route drift was 6 to 15 B in an earlier build of the same tree, which is the size of this machine's own run-to-run noise. Measured 2026-08-30 on Intel Core i7-1265U, 12 logical cores, Windows 11 10.0.26200, node v24.12.0, six sibling agents on the box. It buys the one answer the page could not give: when the site runs out of room. What it removed pays part of it - the size waterfall and the size sparkline are both gone, and so is the Runs and site size table. The engine is NOT in this number. It is a lazy chunk of 585,481 B raw and 197,561 B gzip -9, measured in the same build and byte-identical to the figure this record carried before, because this change added no chart type and no component to src/lib/charts/core.ts. It is fetched only when a chart hydrates and no page preloads it - frontend/tests/charts.spec.ts fails the build if one ever does. The prerendered console document is 179,791 B gzip -9 over the committed ledger, against a ceiling of 301,580, leaving 121,789 spare. Confirm against the CI site job before trusting the absolute figures: a local Windows build has read 81 to 87 B under CI on every route before now.
